metrics.agentOutput:
Done. The report now renders through Markout's source-generated serializer for a Unicode terminal.

**What I changed in `Program.cs`:**
- Annotated `PerfReport` with `[MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))]` so `Title` becomes the H1 rule-bordered heading.
- Marked `Timings` and `Coverage` with `[MarkoutSection(...)]` + `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]`.
- Serialized through a generated context: `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(perf, Console.Out, new UnicodeFormatter(), ReportContext.Default)`, with a `[MarkoutContext(typeof(PerfReport))] partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext`.

**Key decision — built-in shapes:**
- Timings stayed `List<Metric>` → renders as **labeled bars** (Restore/Compile/Test).
- Coverage became `List<Breakdown>` (wrapping the single `Breakdown`/`Slice` data). A *scalar* `Breakdown` was wrongly decomposed into a `Field | Value` table (with a `MARKOUT001` warning); the documented Composition shape is `List<Breakdown>`, which renders as the terminal **breakdown bar**. No hand-built rows.

**Note on the coverage bar:** the core `UnicodeFormatter` draws each breakdown as one proportional bar and distinguishes slices by color only — I confirmed the package emits no ANSI/shade glyphs, so under redirected output it shows as a solid block. That's the library's built-in terminal behavior (the Markdown formatter shows the same data as `Covered 82% / Uncovered 18%`), not something to fix with custom formatting.

Build succeeds with 0 warnings / 0 errors.

1. ---
2. name: markout
3. description: >-
4.   Source-generated .NET serializer that renders objects as Markdown (also ANSI terminal,
5.   plain text, pretty tables, TSV). Reach for it when a CLI or tool needs structured, human-
6.   or agent-readable output instead of hand-built strings. It looks like System.Text.Json
7.   source generation but the rules differ — there is NO reflection fallback, so it requires a
8.   generated MarkoutSerializerContext and Markout-specific attributes. See the body for the
9.   required pattern.
10. ---
11. 
12. # Markout — produce Markdown/structured output from objects
13. 
14. Source-generated serializer. Default output is Markdown. Package `Markout` (includes the
15. source generator; no extra package needed).
16. 
17. ## The required pattern (3 parts — all mandatory)
18. 
19. ```csharp
20. using Markout;
21. 
22. // 1. Annotate every model type. List<T> -> table, scalar -> field.
23. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))]   // TitleProperty -> the H1 heading
24. public class Report
25. {
26.     public string Title { get; set; } = "";
27.     public int Count { get; set; }
28.     [MarkoutSection(Name = "Items")]                    // -> "## Items" heading
29.     public List<Row>? Items { get; set; }              // List<T> -> a table
30. }
31. 
32. [MarkoutSerializable]
33. public class Row { public string Name { get; set; } = ""; public string Value { get; set; } = ""; }
34. 
35. // 2. Register EVERY type on a partial context (the source generator fills it in).
36. [MarkoutContext(typeof(Report))]
37. [MarkoutContext(typeof(Row))]
38. public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { }
39. 
40. // 3. Serialize THROUGH the context.
41. MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default);
42. ```
43. 
44. ## Gotchas (where intuition from System.Text.Json is wrong)
45. 
46. - **No reflection fallback.** There is no `Serialize(obj)` overload. EVERY `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize`
47.   overload takes a `MarkoutSerializerContext` (or `MarkoutTypeInfo<T>`). Skipping the context does
48.   not compile. This is the #1 mistake.
49. - **Register every type.** A model used in output but missing `[MarkoutSerializable]` +
50.   `[MarkoutContext(typeof(T))]` will not serialize. The context class MUST be `partial`.
51. - **Attributes are Markout's, not System.Text.Json's:** `[MarkoutSerializable]` (not
52.   `[JsonSerializable]`), `[MarkoutContext]`, `[MarkoutSection(Name=...)]`, `TitleProperty`,
53.   `[MarkoutPropertyName]`, `[MarkoutIgnore]`. Do not use `Json*` attributes.
54. - **Rendering is driven by type, not markup:** `List<T>` -> table; scalar (`string`/`int`/`bool`) ->
55.   a `Field | Value` row; `[MarkoutSection(Name="X")]` -> a `## X` heading above the property.
56. - **Put `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on non-tabular list properties** (`List<Metric>`, `List<Breakdown>`,
57.   `List<TreeNode>`, `List<Description>`, `Callout`) or they get mistreated as table columns.
58. 
59. ## Built-in shape types (use as model properties for rich output)
60. 
61. `Metric` (bar chart), `Breakdown`/`Slice` (stacked bar), `Callout` (alert), `TreeNode`
62. (hierarchy), `Description` (term + text), `CodeSection` (code block). e.g. `new Metric("Build", 4.2)`.
63. Pass children as a list/array/collection expression, never as trailing arguments:
64. `new TreeNode("root", [new TreeNode("leaf")])`. `Badge` is an optional property:
65. `new TreeNode("root") { Badge = "📁" }`.
66. 
67. ## Composite table cells (dense Markdown + decomposed columns from one model)
68. 
69. Composite cells are data-only scalar properties: `FieldLayout.Table` renders a dense Markdown
70. value, and `TableFormatter` (TSV/JSONL) decomposes each into typed columns from one declaration.
71. 
72. - `Change<V>` — a `before → after` change (NOT `Comparison`, which collides with `System.Comparison<T>`).
73.   `[MarkoutDelta(Delta.Percent)]` on a numeric `Change<V>` appends the signed change, e.g.
74.   `98555 → 61190 (−38%)`; `Delta.Absolute` appends the signed difference; `Delta.Multiple` appends a
75.   multiplicative factor with a direction word, e.g. `15 → 5 (3× fewer)` / `5 → 15 (3× more)` (a zero
76.   endpoint renders `—`). With a goal, an aligned `Delta.Multiple` word omits the redundant status word
77.   (`15 → 5 (3× fewer)` under `Goal.Lower`); a conflicting one keeps it (`5 → 15 (3× more, bad)`).
78.   `[MarkoutDeltaNoun("solved")]` renders a caller noun on the signed delta —
79.   `4/6 → 6/6 (+2 solved)` (sibling of `[MarkoutUnit]`; composites use `IDeltaCountable`: `Fraction`→count,
80.   `Share`→value; Markdown-only).
81.   `[MarkoutGoal(Goal.Higher)]` / `[MarkoutGoal(Goal.Lower)]` on a numeric `Change<V>` makes Markout
82.   derive two decomposed fields — a structural `direction`
83.   (`increased`/`decreased`/`introduced` (0→N)/`resolved` (N→0)/`unchanged`) and a goal-applied polarity
84.   `status` (`good`/`bad`/`neutral`) — instead of the caller hand-coding ceiling/floor/drift. Optional
85.   noise, `[MarkoutGoal(Goal.Higher, 0.001)]`, treats sub-threshold movement as `unchanged`. `Goal.Context`
86.   (default) derives nothing. Composite `Change<Share|Percent|Fraction>` also derive `direction`/`status`
87.   from a single comparable magnitude (`Share` → raw `Value`; `Percent`/`Fraction` → their ratio;
88.   `Segments` → the **sum** of its parts' values, i.e. the breakdown total). In dense Markdown the polarity word
89.   renders inline, merged with any delta suffix into one group: `0 → 7 (bad)`, `98555 → 61190 (−38%, good)`.
90. - `Fraction(count, total)` → `24/24`; `Share(value, whole)` → `5056 (24%)`
91.   (`[MarkoutUnit("s")]` → `103s (93%)`); `Percent(part, whole)` → `93%`;
92.   `Segments(new Segment(label, value), ...)` → `21/171/236` (labels become column names).
93. - `Change<V>` nests over composites: `Change<Fraction>`, `Change<Share>`, `Change<Segments>`.
94.   A zero denominator renders `—` rather than `NaN`/`Inf`. e.g.
95.   `[MarkoutPropertyName("Session IET"), MarkoutDelta(Delta.Percent)] public Change<long> SessionIet { get; init; }`.
96. 
97. JSONL decomposition is **heterogeneous** (each record holds only its own keys); TSV keeps a uniform
98. column union (absent cells blank). Set `MarkoutWriterOptions.JsonTypedValues = true` to emit numeric
99. columns as JSON numbers instead of strings.
100. 
101. When a composite cell (`Change<V>`, etc.) is a **column of an element table** (`List<T>` where `T` has a
102. composite property), structured formatters (TSV/JSONL) **decompose it into typed `{column}_{sub}` columns**
103. — `score_before`/`score_after`/`score_delta_pct`, `bugs_direction`/`bugs_status`, `tasks_delta_count`/
104. `tasks_delta_noun` — so the card is reconstructable from the data. Markdown keeps the dense cell
105. (`100 → 50 (-50%)`). Scalar columns and Markdown are unchanged. `[MarkoutIgnoreColumnWhen]` columns that
106. are hidden for the table are dropped from the decomposed output too.
107. 
108. ## Card shapes (declare a list; the generator picks the layout)
109. 
110. Two list-shapes render as multi-format cards from a `[MarkoutSerializable]` model — Markdown table +
111. flat typed JSONL/TSV — with no imperative writer calls:
112. 
113. - `List<MetricChange<T>>` — a gated scalar metric per row. `MetricChange<T>(Name, Before, After,
114.   Target? = null, TargetLabel? = null, Status = GateStatus.Unknown, StatusLabel? = null)` where
115.   `T : struct`. Set `{ Goal = Goal.Higher|Lower }` (init property; optionally `Noise`) to derive the
116.   `direction`/`status` axes from `Before → After`; a caller-supplied `Status` overrides the derived
117.   polarity. **Dense Markdown (default):** `Metric | Change | Target` with the status word inlined
118.   (`0 → 7 (bad)` — caller `StatusLabel` wins over the slug) and a goal marker on the label
119.   (`Failures (-)` / `Fully raised (+)`); the `Status` column is dropped. Set
120.   `MarkoutWriterOptions.InlineGoalStatus = false` for the legacy `Metric | Change | Target | Status`.
121.   JSONL/TSV are unaffected: flat `before`/`after`/optional `target`/`target_label`/`direction`/`status`.
122.   `T` must be a numeric scalar (int/long/double/decimal/...); a composite `T` (e.g. `Segments`) is a
123.   compile error (`MARKOUT005`).
124. - `[MarkoutSection(Name = "...", IncludeSectionInStructuredRows = true)]` on a `List<MetricChange<T>>`
125.   or `List<MultiSourceRow>` section prepends a leading `section` column (the section name) to TSV/JSONL
126.   rows — for multiplexing several sectioned card shapes into one structured stream. Markdown is unchanged.
127. - `List<MultiSourceRow>` — a role matrix: `MultiSourceRow(label, params Source[])`,
128.   `Source(role, IMarkoutCell? value, format = default)`. Roles pivot to **columns** in Markdown
129.   (caller-supplied order; absent role → `-`); JSONL emits one flat record per row with
130.   `{role}_{side}_{field}` keys. Values are any `IMarkoutCell` incl. nested `Change<Share>` etc.;
131.   **scalars work too** — `new Source("baseline", 2)` (int/long/double/decimal) and `Source.Text(role, s)`
132.   decompose to a single `{role}` field; `new Source(role, null)` is an absent cell. Set the label column
133.   header with `[MarkoutLabelHeader("Metric")]` (defaults to `Field`).
134. - `Verdict(GateStatus Status, string? Label = null)` — a first-class verdict cell (typed polarity
135.   `GateStatus` + optional caller label); use as a `Source` value for a verdict row (decomposes to `{role}`).
136. 
137. Decomposition keys are `snake_case_lower` (a fused role like `claude-opus-4.8` becomes
138. `claude_opus_4_8_...`). Put `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on these lists only when nested inside a table.
139. 
140. ## Other output formats (still Markdown by default)
141. 
142. Pass a formatter to change output: `new MarkdownFormatter()` (default), `PlainTextFormatter`,
143. `UnicodeFormatter`, `TableFormatter` (compact/TSV/JSONL via `MarkoutWriterOptions.TableMode`).
144. e.g. `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ReportContext.Default);`
145.

## The required pattern (3 parts — all mandatory)

using Markout;

// 1. Annotate every model type. List<T> -> table, scalar -> field.
[MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))]   // TitleProperty -> the H1 heading
public class Report
{
    public string Title { get; set; } = "";
    public int Count { get; set; }                     // scalar -> "Count | 3" field row
    [MarkoutSection(Name = "Items")]                   // -> "## Items" heading

```

## Scalar field shaping (title, description, per-value formatting)

Shape scalar properties with attributes — never pre-format strings in the model or hand-write rows:

```csharp
[MarkoutSerializable(
    TitleProperty = nameof(Name),               // -> the H1 heading
    DescriptionProperty = nameof(Summary),      // -> a paragraph under the H1 (NOT a Field | Value row)
    FieldLayout = FieldLayout.Inline)]          // Table (default) | Inline | Bulleted | Numbered | Plain
public class Component
{
    public string Name { get; set; } = "";
    public string Summary { get; set; } = "";

    [MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:N0} downloads")]  // 5100000 -> "5,100,000 downloads"
    public long Downloads { get; set; }

    [MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:yyyy-MM-dd}")]    // DateTime -> "2024-06-01"
    public DateTime Published { get; set; }

    [MarkoutBoolFormat("Yes", "No")]            // true -> "Yes", false -> "No"
    public bool Verified { get; set; }
}
```

- `DescriptionProperty` renders a property as a description paragraph, not a table row.
- `FieldLayout.Inline` puts the scalar fields on one line (`Owner: … | Status: …`) instead of a table.
- `[MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:…}")]` / `[MarkoutBoolFormat(t,f)]` format a value **in place** — do not bake
  the formatting into the getter or build the cell string yourself.

## Gotchas (where System.Text.Json intuition is wrong)

- **No reflection fallback.** There is no `Serialize(obj)` overload. EVERY `Serialize` call takes a
  `MarkoutSerializerContext`. Omitting it does not compile — the #1 mistake.
- **Register every type.** A model missing `[MarkoutSerializable]` + `[MarkoutContext(typeof(T))]`
  won't serialize. The context class MUST be `partial`.
- **Markout attributes, not Json:** `[MarkoutSerializable]` (not `[JsonSerializable]`),
  `[MarkoutContext]`, `[MarkoutSection(Name=...)]`, `[MarkoutPropertyName]`, `[MarkoutIgnore]`.
- **Type drives rendering, not markup:** `List<T>` -> table; scalar -> `Field | Value` row;
  `[MarkoutSection(Name="X")]` -> a `## X` heading above the property.
- **`[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on non-tabular list properties** (`List<Metric>`, `List<Breakdown>`,
  `List<TreeNode>`, `List<Description>`, `Callout`) or they get mistreated as table columns.

## Most common workflow: JSON API → model → report

Fetch JSON, project to a Markout model (a plain data model is fine — no separate visual layer),
serialize. Keep the JSON DTO and the Markout model separate; project between them with LINQ.

- **conditional-composition** — show/hide sections & columns from the data; filter to sections;

# Output formats — one model, many formats

Default `Serialize(...)` emits Markdown. Pass a **formatter** (and optional `MarkoutWriterOptions`)
to get other formats. The anti-pattern is per-format string building (`string.Join("\t", ...)`); let
Markout project the same model to each format so columns/headers stay consistent.

## Formatters

```csharp
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(r, Console.Out, ctx);                              // Markdown (default)
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(r, Console.Out, new MarkdownFormatter(), ctx);     // Markdown, explicit
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(r, Console.Out, new PlainTextFormatter(), ctx);    // plain text / logs (ASCII, no pipes)
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(r, Console.Out, new UnicodeFormatter(), ctx);      // Unicode box-drawing tables
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(r, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ctx);        // compact pretty rows

using Markout.Ansi.Spectre;                                                    // extra package
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(r, Console.Out, new SpectreFormatter(AnsiConsole.Console), ctx); // ANSI
```

`Markout.Ansi.Spectre` is a separate NuGet package; Markdown/plain/table/TSV/JSONL need only `Markout`.

## TableFormatter modes + writer options

`TableFormatter` + `MarkoutWriterOptions.TableMode` selects the tabular shape:

```csharp
var opts = new MarkoutWriterOptions
{
    TableMode = MarkoutTableMode.Tsv,          // Pretty | Tsv | Jsonl
    IncludeDescription = false,
    IncludeSections = new HashSet<string> { "Results" },
    JsonTypedValues = true,                    // JSONL/TSV: emit numbers as numbers, not quoted
    MaxItems = 3,                              // cap rows; appends a "... and {N} more" notice
};
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ctx, opts);
```

- `MarkoutTableMode.Pretty` — columns aligned to a uniform start position.
- `MarkoutTableMode.Tsv` — stable `snake_case` headers; never emits embedded tabs/newlines in cells.
- `MarkoutTableMode.Jsonl` — one record per row (heterogeneous keys; see composite-cells-cards).
- `MaxItems = N` caps EVERY table to N rows and appends `... and {count} more`; works with any formatter,
  so a Markdown view can show the first N rows while TSV/JSONL export them all. (Or per-property:
  `[MarkoutMaxItems(3)]`, with an optional `EllipsisFormat`.)

## Central multi-format dispatch (the CLI `--format` pattern)

Route one model through one method so every command gets every format for free:

```csharp
static void Render<TView, TJson>(TView view, OutputFormat fmt, MarkoutSerializerContext ctx)
{
    switch (fmt)
    {
        case OutputFormat.Text:  MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(view, Console.Out, new PlainTextFormatter(), ctx); break;
        case OutputFormat.Md:    MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(view, Console.Out, new MarkdownFormatter(), ctx,
                                     new MarkoutWriterOptions { MaxItems = 3 }); break;   // first 3 rows + "... and N more"
        case OutputFormat.Table: MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(view, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ctx); break;
        case OutputFormat.Tsv:   MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(view, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ctx,
                                     new MarkoutWriterOptions { TableMode = MarkoutTableMode.Tsv }); break;
        case OutputFormat.Jsonl: MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(view, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ctx,
                                     new MarkoutWriterOptions { TableMode = MarkoutTableMode.Jsonl, JsonTypedValues = true }); break;
    }
}
```

keep Markout for the structured formats — don't try to force it.

- Markdown table cells normalize `|` to `|` (not `\|`).
- TSV uses stable `snake_case` headers and never embeds tabs/newlines in cells.
- Pretty renders the same projection as TSV, aligned.

- One model → many formats; never hand-assemble TSV/JSONL rows.

- **Rendering is driven by type, not markup:** `List<T>` -> table; scalar (`string`/`int`/`bool`) ->
  a `Field | Value` row; `[MarkoutSection(Name="X")]` -> a `## X` heading above the property.
- **Put `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on non-tabular list properties** (`List<Metric>`, `List<Breakdown>`,
  `List<TreeNode>`, `List<Description>`, `Callout`) or they get mistreated as table columns.

## Built-in shape types (use as model properties for rich output)

`Metric` (bar chart), `Breakdown`/`Slice` (stacked bar), `Callout` (alert), `TreeNode`
(hierarchy), `Description` (term + text), `CodeSection` (code block). e.g. `new Metric("Build", 4.2)`.
Pass children as a list/array/collection expression, never as trailing arguments:
`new TreeNode("root", [new TreeNode("leaf")])`. `Badge` is an optional property:
`new TreeNode("root") { Badge = "📁" }`.

## Composite table cells (dense Markdown + decomposed columns from one model)

Composite cells are data-only scalar properties: `FieldLayout.Table` renders a dense Markdown
value, and `TableFormatter` (TSV/JSONL) decomposes each into typed columns from one declaration.

- `Change<V>` — a `before → after` change (NOT `Comparison`, which collides with `System.Comparison<T>`).
  `[MarkoutDelta(Delta.Percent)]` on a numeric `Change<V>` appends the signed change, e.g.
  `98555 → 61190 (−38%)`; `Delta.Absolute` appends the signed difference; `Delta.Multiple` appends a
  multiplicative factor with a direction word, e.g. `15 → 5 (3× fewer)` / `5 → 15 (3× more)` (a zero
  endpoint renders `—`). With a goal, an aligned `Delta.Multiple` word omits the redundant status word
--
  (default) derives nothing. Composite `Change<Share|Percent|Fraction>` also derive `direction`/`status`
  from a single comparable magnitude (`Share` → raw `Value`; `Percent`/`Fraction` → their ratio;
  `Segments` → the **sum** of its parts' values, i.e. the breakdown total). In dense Markdown the polarity word
  renders inline, merged with any delta suffix into one group: `0 → 7 (bad)`, `98555 → 61190 (−38%, good)`.
- `Fraction(count, total)` → `24/24`; `Share(value, whole)` → `5056 (24%)`
  (`[MarkoutUnit("s")]` → `103s (93%)`); `Percent(part, whole)` → `93%`;
  `Segments(new Segment(label, value), ...)` → `21/171/236` (labels become column names).
- `Change<V>` nests over composites: `Change<Fraction>`, `Change<Share>`, `Change<Segments>`.
  A zero denominator renders `—` rather than `NaN`/`Inf`. e.g.
  `[MarkoutPropertyName("Session IET"), MarkoutDelta(Delta.Percent)] public Change<long> SessionIet { get; init; }`.

JSONL decomposition is **heterogeneous** (each record holds only its own keys); TSV keeps a uniform
column union (absent cells blank). Set `MarkoutWriterOptions.JsonTypedValues = true` to emit numeric
columns as JSON numbers instead of strings.

When a composite cell (`Change<V>`, etc.) is a **column of an element table** (`List<T>` where `T` has a
composite property), structured formatters (TSV/JSONL) **decompose it into typed `{column}_{sub}` columns**
